newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's KGHM buys majority stake in cable-maker.
newsitem.headline: Poland's KGHM buys majority stake in cable-maker.

text.p: Poland's KGHM copper concern has bought 17 percent of shares of the country's biggest cable maker Krakowska Fabryka Kabli (KFK) raising its stake to above 51 percent, a KFK official said.

Deputy KFK president Hubert Irzenski told Reuter KGHM's subsidary KGHM Metale SA, which previously had 34 percent in KFK, bought 9.8 percent of employee shares and seven percent from Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy SA BPH.
"KGHM Metale has bought shares from employees and BPH which give it a 51 percent stake in KFK," Irzenski said. @
Last year KFK, which employs 2,143 people, had a net profit of 13.5 million zlotys on sales of 395.5 million.
KGHM Metale also has a 26 percent stake in a cable factory in Zalom near the port od Szczecin and owns the small Elpena cable maker.

Before the employee share buy-back the biggest shareholder in KFK was the trading conglomerate Elektrim which has 42.55 percent in the firm. the remaining shares are in the hands of small investors. @
Irzenski said KGHM agreed not to take dividend for five years and invest in the modernisation of the company.
